back: Hitler's aim of winning 'living space' in eastern Europe, especially in the Soviet Union, for German settlement.
The secret state police, created by Göring in Prussia in 1933 and later controlled by Himmler; it arrested without trial and relied on informers.

front: What was the Reich Chamber of Culture?
back: The body, created in September 1933 under Goebbels, which writers, artists, musicians and broadcasters had to join in order to work.

front: When did German troops enter the Rhineland?
back: March 1936, breaking the Treaty of Versailles and Locarno; Britain and France did not act.
The union of Germany and Austria in March 1938.
Colonel von Stauffenberg's bomb failed to kill Hitler; the plotters were executed.

front: When was the Nazi-Soviet Pact signed?
back: 23 August 1939; it cleared the way for the invasion of Poland on 1 September.

front: Why did propaganda succeed in Nazi Germany?
back: It reinforced existing beliefs, such as hatred of Versailles, used all the media, and was backed by economic and foreign policy successes.

front: Why was there so little opposition to Hitler?
back: Terror and informers, divisions among opponents, popularity of the regime and the army's oath of loyalty.

front: Was Hitler's foreign policy planned or opportunistic?
back: Intentionalists see a consistent programme; Taylor stressed opportunism; most historians see consistent aims with flexible methods.
